'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and cultural heritage]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
**The [[Archaeological Survey of India]] closes all [[monument]]s, [[museum]]s, and protected sites until May 15 due to an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/travel/travel-news/archaeological-survey-of-india-closes-all-of-its-sites-until-may-15/as82099968.cms (''The Times of India'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey|Turkish Central Bank]] bans transactions using [[Cryptocurrency|cryptocurrencies]] and crypto assets, citing possible "irreparable damage" and transaction risks to customers. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/4/16/turkey-bans-crypto-payments-and-bitcoin-feels-the-pain (Al Jazeera)]
  
'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] receives her first dose of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/angelamerkel-gets-her-astrazeneca-covid-vaccine-shot/a-57222191 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Russia]]
*****The number of [[Russians]] vaccinated against COVID-19 surpasses eight million. [https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/71600/ (Interfax)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 63,082 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4,150,039. [https://in.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-turkey/turkey-logs-highest-daily-covid-19-cases-since-pandemic-began-idINKBN2C3277 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] receives 117,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.unicef.org/ukraine/en/press-releases/covax-arrival-ukraine (UNICEF)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[Scotland]] relaxes its COVID-19-related restrictions, allowing non-essential travel around the country and some social gatherings. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-56765188 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****[[Ontario]] [[Premier of Ontario|Premier]] [[Doug Ford]] announces a six-week extension of the [[stay-at-home order]] with new restrictions until May 20, including a ban of outdoor gatherings outside the household, as the COVID-19 cases remain high. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/covid-19-ontario-april-16-2021-new-restrictions-modelling-1.5990092 (CBC)]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]]
*****[[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] says [[Pfizer]] will double the amounts of [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] that are being shipped to [[Canada]]. He also announces that the [[Canadian Red Cross]] will be deployed to [[Ontario]] to help with [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccinations]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pandemics-toronto-ontario-justin-trudeau-coronavirus-pandemic-30d370ec5cdd11036bed9cea8057e64b (AP)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
*****[[Premier of British Columbia|British Columbia Premier]] [[John Horgan]] receives his first dose of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[vaccine]]. [https://vancouversun.com/news/covid-19-premier-john-horgan-set-to-roll-up-his-sleeve-for-the-astrazeneca-jab (''Vancouver Sun'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] says that 200 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine have been administered. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-16/u-s-vaccinations-reach-200-million-as-campaign-picks-up-speed (Bloomberg.com)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****[[Michigan]] extends its restrictions on gatherings and dining to May 24 due to an increase in the number of cases. The state also expands its [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] to children. [https://www.freep.com/story/news/health/2021/04/16/michigan-covid-19-health-order-kid/7234835002/ (''Detroit Free Press'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Virginia]], [[Lineage P.1]]
*****[[Virginia]] reports its first two cases of the Lineage P.1 variant, which was originally detected in [[Brazil]]. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-virginia-164cb227d8cdff55f135374d419d5f38 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 101 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 10,181. [https://www.thenationalherald.com/coronavirus/arthro/bangladesh_recorded_101_new_covid_19_deaths-2223022/ (''The National Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports a record 217,353 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 14.29 million. The country also reports 1,185 deaths, which is the highest daily total since September, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 174,308. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-records-217-353-covid-19-cases-in-highest-ever-daily-spike-101618543381875.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Government of Japan|government]] designates [[Aichi Prefecture|Aichi]], [[Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa]], [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]], and [[Saitama Prefecture|Saitama]] prefectures for tougher measures that would require restaurants and bars to close at 8:00 p.m. between April 20 and May 15. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20210415/p2g/00m/0na/091000c (''The Mainichi'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] announces the closure of educational institutions, pubs, bars, karaoke shops, and massage parlours; a ban on alcohol sales at restaurants; and a ban on gatherings of more than 50 people for at least two weeks, beginning April 18, due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2100707/no-curfew-gatherings-banned-for-2-weeks (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] reports a record 29,472 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total to 2,658,574 cases. [https://www.clarin.com/sociedad/coronavirus-argentina-reportan-29-472-casos-nuevos-nuevo-record-contagios-dia_0_oQlikoA-W.html (''Clarín'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tonga]]
***[[Salote Mafileʻo Pilolevu Tuita]], Princess of [[Tonga]], received her first dose of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]], thereby becoming the first person to be vaccinated against COVID-19 in the disease-free country. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/440580/tonga-s-princess-takes-the-lead-on-covid-19-vaccination (RNZ)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**The [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian Foreign Minister]] says that [[Moscow]] will ask ten U.S. [[diplomat]]s to leave [[Russia]] in retaliation to expulsions of Russian diplomats ordered by the [[United States]] yesterday. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-eastern-europe-diplomacy-moscow-foreign-policy-5cf0a7f222668db3fe432f0db599868c (AP)]
*[[United States involvement in regime change]], [[Cuba–United States relations]]
**Declassified documents released by the [[National Security Archive]] show that the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] was involved in a plot to assassinate [[Raúl Castro]] in 1960. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/cia-plan-assassinate-raul-castro-1960-declassified-pilot-14639816 (CNA)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Criminal proceedings in the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Criminal charges brought in the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
***American guitarist and [[Oath Keepers]] member [[Jon Schaffer]] pleads guilty for his role in the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]], thus making him the first participant in the [[riot]] to do so. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/16/politics/oath-keepers-capitol-guilty-plea-schaffer/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*In a widely-expected move at the [[Congress of the Communist Party of Cuba|8th Congress of the Communist Party]], [[Raúl Castro]] officially resigns as [[First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba|First Secretary]], the most powerful position in [[Cuba]]. Incumbent [[President of Cuba|President]] [[Miguel Díaz-Canel]] is expected to succeed him. [http://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/cuba-raul-castro-steps-head-communist-party-rcna689 (NBC News)]

*[[Artemis program]]
**[[NASA]] awards [[SpaceX]] a contract to build its next-generation [[Artemis program#Human Landing System|Human Landing System]] to return American [[astronaut]]s to the [[lunar surface]] during this decade. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-56781556 (BBC News)]
